note: For a regex magic rule, the input-controlled buffer range beginning at the rule offset is stored as the search string used by the regex matcher.
The input-controlled search length bounds how many bytes are copied and presented to regexec.
The match result object is allocated without initialization before calling the regex wrapper.
The code relies on a successful regexec call to initialize pmatch, but the vulnerable runtime can return success while leaving pmatch fields uninitialized for this regex path.
After rc is zero, libmagic consumes pmatch.rm_so; if regexec left it uninitialized, MemorySanitizer reports an uninitialized read here.
